mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to tightened near-term discount rates depressing expected equity valuations.
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 20-day forward returns during Fed rate hikes are not statistically different from the prior month's returns (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly UNRATE falls by more than 0.2 percentage points in a month, labor market slack increases, reducing expected corporate profit margins and producing a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: During periods where UNRATE declines > 0.2% monthly, the 60-day forward return is positive in >70% of instances (empirical frequency test).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both HOUST (industrial production) and GDPC1 (personal consumption) above their prior month's levels, with no simultaneous decline in INDPRO, predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals robust overall economic demand.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month AND GDPC1 > previous month AND INDPRO ≤ previous month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative despite the signal in >50% of similar trigger events (frequency test).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of at least 2% for three consecutive months indicates weakening supply-side conditions, which is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate future demand absorption.
failure_condition: No significant positive 60-day forward return occurs during any 12-month window of INDPRO ≤ -2% for 3 consecutive months (time-series regression p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for two consecutive months, the persistence of low short-term rates is associated with a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as markets anticipate future rate cuts.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is negative in all instances where the trigger is met (empirical frequency = 0%).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in PAYEMS (employment) exceeding 5% month-over-month in a month when UNRATE is below 3% signals a tight labor market, which precedes a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as wage pressures weigh on inflation expectations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month by >5% AND UNRATE < 3%
failure_condition: During such triggers, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from the prior month's return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both CPIAUCSL (inflation) and HOUST (production) by at least 0.5% suggests cooling demand and cost pressures, which predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive in >50% of similar events (frequency test).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE rises by more than 0.4% in a month and INDPRO remains flat for two months, it indicates a shift toward higher wage costs without additional supply, which is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE month-over-month > 0.4% AND INDPRO month-over-month ≤ previous month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not negative in >70% of such trigger events (empirical frequency test).
